newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 to $10 higher as dealers awaited the release of the U.S. first quarter cocoa grind.
Most market operators were looking for the grind to come in unchanged to slightly higher against year-ago levels. The data are due out at 0845 EST/1245 GMT.
Thursday, CSCE cocoa ended firmer but well below session highs. Most-active July closed up $12 at $1,451 a tonne after topping out at resistance at $1,480.
In London, July futures were 3 stg a tonne lower at the midday break Friday, at 1036 stg per tonne.
Technically, July near-term support was seen at last Friday's low of $1,433. To the upside, resistance was pegged at $1,457-$1,459, with a large chart gap looming at $1,480-1,504.
For U.S. first-quarter grind data, analysts' forecasts ranged from flat to up five percent.
